property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets baseToken to address(0) unconditionally and thus violates this when _baseToken != address(0).

For any initialize(...) call the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the provided _baseToken argument (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken); the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets baseToken equal to the supplied _baseToken argument; the mutant erroneously sets baseToken to the supplied _nft argument, so for some fuzzed inputs the stored baseToken will differ from the _baseToken parameter (causing the property to fail).

For any inputs to initialize, the correct contract sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken (so c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize returns), whereas the mutant that omits assigning baseToken will leave c.baseToken() unchanged for some inputs (i.e. c.baseToken() != _baseToken).

For any caller and any initialize(...) arguments, the reference contract always sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken parameter; the mutant overrides baseToken with msg.sender, so there exist inputs (when msg.sender != _baseToken) where baseToken differs after initialize.

After initialize(...) completes, the contract's nft getter returns exactly the address passed as the _nft argument; the mutant assigns nft = _baseToken so for some inputs nft() != the _nft argument and thus violates this rule.

For any initialize(...) call, the contract's public nft() must equal the _nft argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets nft to Factory(factory).ownerOf(address(this)) instead, so for some inputs nft() != _nft and the property is violated.

For any inputs, after initialize(...) succeeds the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument provided; the mutant derives nft from the factory owner instead, causing nft() != _nft for some inputs.

For any call to initialize(...) that succeeds, the contract's public nft() must equal the _nft argument passed; the mutant instead sets nft to Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) and therefore for some inputs (when Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) differs from the provided _nft) nft() != _nft, causing the property to fail.

For all inputs, calling initialize(...) should set the public nft() to the provided _nft argument; the mutant instead reads the nft from Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) which can differ from the provided _nft for some inputs, so the property will fail on the mutant.

For any inputs to initialize, after a successful call the contract's public nft() must equal the address passed in as the _nft parameter; the mutant derives nft from Factory(factory).ownerOf(uint160(address(this))) instead and therefore for some factory owner values the stored nft() differs, causing the property to be violated.
For any inputs to initialize, the stored changeFee equals the provided _changeFee (i.e. c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant increments the stored value breaking this equality for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument passed (i.e., initialize preserves the provided changeFee); the mutant sets changeFee to zero causing this to differ for some nonzero _changeFee inputs.

For any initialize(...) call the contract stores changeFee equal to the provided _changeFee; the mutant overrides that and stores uint56.max instead, so the stored changeFee will differ for some inputs (any _changeFee != type(uint56).max).

For any uint16 feeRate input ≤ 5000 passed to initialize, the deployed contract's public feeRate equals that input (reference); the mutant ignores the input and sets feeRate to 100, so the property will fail for inputs != 100.

For any inputs passed to initialize, the correct contract sets feeRate equal to the _feeRate argument before emitting Initialize (so the public getter feeRate() equals the argument immediately after initialize returns); the mutant that assigns feeRate after setting initialized=true can be observed because a reentrant attacker can call back during initialization and observe initialized==true while feeRate still equals zero (or not equal to the provided _feeRate), violating the invariant that feeRate() == _feeRate after successful initialize.

For any inputs to initialize, after initialize returns successfully the contract's public feeRate() equals the _feeRate argument; the mutant that assigns feeRate after setting initialized=true can be reentrancy-attacked during initialize so an external caller observing state during initialization can see initialized==true but feeRate != _feeRate, thus there exist inputs (an attacker contract performing a reentrant call in its onERC721Received or in receive) that make the mutant violate the invariant.
